title: Externality Mushrooms — public goods grove
description: Two agents on a 24×24 grid harvest mushrooms with a public-goods structure. selfish_mushroom (red) gives +2 to the picker only. public_mushroom (golden) gives +1 to the picker but **+3 to each other agent** as a positive externality (the canonical public good). Each pickup IS the cooperation/defection action — no encounter mechanic, payoff accrues directly. Mushrooms respawn 6 turns after pickup. The decision space is a canonical PD: T=5 > R=4 > P=2 > S=1 with 2R > T+S, but the mutual-cooperation social total (8) is double the mutual-defection total (4). The `say` verb is allowed and tracked (cheap-talk variant — same convention as prisoners_dilemma_01).
goal: Maximize cumulative score across 60 turns by harvesting mushrooms. There are TWO mushroom types with very different incentive structures: (1) selfish_mushroom — pickup gives +2 to picker only, no benefit to anyone else; (2) public_mushroom — pickup gives +1 to picker but +3 to each other agent (positive externality, public good). The choice between them per pickup is the cooperation/defection action. Round-trip PD payoffs: T=5 > R=4 > P=2 > S=1 (canonical PD, 2R > T+S). Mutual cooperation pareto-dominates mutual defection in social total (8 vs 4 per round-trip). The `say` verb is allowed and transmitted. Mushrooms respawn 6 turns after pickup.
notes: Sprint 2 P6 from project_sprint_plan_paper.md (2026-05-01). MeltingPot 'Externality Mushrooms: Dense' family lineage — sixth Blockworld MeltingPot-comparable scenario after stag_hunt_01 / stag_hunt_repeated_01 / commons_harvest_01 / predator_prey_01 / pure_coord_01 / prisoners_dilemma_01. Closes Sprint 2 substrate fills.

Token layout: 4 selfish_mushrooms at corners (4,4)(19,4)(4,19)(19,19), 4 public_mushrooms at midpoints (12,4)(12,19)(6,12)(17,12). Symmetric — both agents equidistant from one selfish + one public mushroom in each direction.
Payoff calibration: selfish=2, public_self=1, public_other=3 → canonical PD with T=5, R=4, P=2, S=1. 2R=8 > T+S=6 (no exploitation incentive larger than cooperation total).

Distinction from prisoners_dilemma_01: PD-in-matrix uses encounter-time inventory ratio (indirect, requires meeting). Externality Mushrooms makes EACH pickup the cooperation/defection action (direct, no encounter). Higher decision frequency, finer-grained behavioral signal.

Behavioral metrics for paper: public_pick_ratio per agent (cooperation rate), externality_received per agent (free-rider detection), score divergence (exploitation signal), say_attempts (cheap-talk usage), pickup time-series (does cooperation decay or stabilize?). Outcome enum: 'mostly_cooperative' (≥70% public picks), 'mostly_selfish' (≤30%), 'mixed', 'asymmetric_exploitation' (one agent zero public picks while other ≥2), 'no_pickups'.

Comparison axis with commons_harvest_01: both are public-goods substrates but commons_harvest is a SHARED resource (depletion → common loss), externality_mushrooms is INDIVIDUAL choice with externality (no shared pool).
